coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 6–8 miles, Z2 only (130–145 bpm), no vert push. You're 15 days out and your recovery score is 60—moderate, not ideal. Your resting HR dropped to 58 (vs. 30-day avg of 65.8), which signals some fatigue accumulation despite lighter volume this week. Thursday is your second recovery day in the taper; treat it as such. This is the phase where you preserve leg freshness and CNS capacity, not build anything. Keep it conversational, flat terrain preferred, 60–65 min easy.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Your sleep last night was 5.69 hours at 69.5% efficiency—below your 30-day average of 8.04h. That deficit matters two weeks out. Prioritize carb repletion after today's easy run: 60–80g carbs + 20g protein within 30 min (rice, banana, Greek yogurt or equivalent). Don't restrict calories in taper; underfeeding now with poor sleep compounds fatigue. Hydrate consistently throughout the day; travel schedule often dehydrates. Aim for 3–4L water baseline plus electrolytes if you're moving between time zones.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep is your leak. Five-and-a-half hours won't cut it 15 days from a 50K. Target 8+ hours tonight—non-negotiable. Use your travel routine to create friction against screen time after 21:00. If jet lag or work stress is the culprit, get afternoon sunlight and consider melatonin 30 min before your target bedtime. Your resting HR improvement is positive, but sustained short sleep will undermine that adaptation. Recovery score of 60 means you're not yet in the green; sleep quality is your highest-ROI lever right now.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're in the psychological gauntlet of the taper: the fitness is there, the volume has dropped, and doubt creeps in. Resist the urge to add mileage or intensity to 'test' your form. The Julian Alps 50K is 2,500m of vert in a sparse-aid environment—that rewards efficiency and pacing discipline, not last-minute heroics. Use these 15 days to visualize race segments (Kranjska Gora start, aid station logistics, final descent), review your nutrition strategy, and mentally rehearse adverse scenarios (stomach issues, weather, bonking). Your mind will be sharper than your legs two weeks out; use it.
